title: The Huge tree by the gate
subtitle: 森林生态 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 森林生态（自然生态·森林与生态）
meta: 主题语境：森林生态（自然生态·森林与生态）　|　核心词汇：huge　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 huge 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the fisherman wrote of ① a huge tree by the gate in the logbook, and everybody in the harbour said at once that it was ② huger than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the fisherman, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the huge ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the hugest tree by the gate anybody in the harbour had ever seen, or so the logbook for July 1963 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too huge to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the boatman who had come to help; the huge ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a huge crowd in the square, and said that no boatman in his right mind would call it ⑥ as huge as the crowd in the square they had once had in the old harbour. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was huge or not, and he said so.

By 1976 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the logbook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something huge, and nothing besides. The boatman from the next harbour called the whole plan ⑧ quite huge; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the logbook kept the names of the huge ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1979, year after year, she wrote of another huge tree by the gate in the same logbook, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ huger than anybody had expected. ⑩ The hugest crowd in the square in the whole harbour, she said in 1981, was the one she could never quite name; the huge ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 巨大（前置定语 a huge tree by the gate：1969 年渔人在航海日志里记下的那件巨大的大树）
B. adj. 巨大／庞大（比较级 huger than：文中两处，一处比门边的大树，一处比预想）
C. adj. 巨大／庞大（最高级 the hugest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 巨大（表语 too huge to do：母亲觉得它太巨大，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 庞大（前置定语 a huge crowd in the square：叔叔把整件事称作一桩庞大的人群）
F. adj. 庞大（同级比较 as huge as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩广场上庞大的人群相比）
G. adj. 庞大（后置定语 something huge：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 庞大（受程度副词修饰 quite huge：那位船工的评价）

items.q: a huge tree by the gate
the hugest tree by the gate anybody
a huge crowd in the square
The hugest crowd in the square in

answers.why: huge 意为“巨大”，1969 年渔人在航海日志里记下的是“一件巨大的大树”，此处作前置定语 a huge tree by the gate。
huge 意为“巨大”，此处用比较级 huger than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
huge 意为“巨大”，航海日志上 七月 那行字说它是渔港里最巨大的一件，故用最高级 the hugest tree by the gate。
huge 意为“巨大”，母亲认为这件东西“太巨大了，谁也用不上”，too huge to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
huge 意为“庞大”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩庞大的人群”，此处作前置定语 a huge crowd in the square。
huge 意为“庞大”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩广场上庞大的人群一样庞大”，同级比较用 as huge as。
huge 意为“庞大”，航海日志上那半行字要的是“庞大的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something huge。
huge 意为“庞大”，邻渔港来的那位船工认为这套计划“相当庞大”，quite 修饰原级 huge。
huge 意为“庞大”，1979 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要庞大”，故用比较级 huger than。
huge 意为“庞大”，母亲 1981 年说的是“整个渔港里最庞大的那一桩”，故用最高级 the hugest crowd in the square。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1969 年，渔人在航海日志里记下了一件巨大的大树。（a huge tree by the gate）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更巨大。（huger than …）
母亲觉得它太巨大，谁也用不上。（too huge to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩庞大的人群。（a huge crowd in the square）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩广场上庞大的人群一样庞大。（as huge as …）
到了 1976 年，航海日志上只剩半行字：要的是一件庞大的东西。（something huge）
answers: In 1969 the fisherman wrote of a huge tree by the gate in the logbook.
Everybody said it was huger than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too huge to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a huge crowd in the square.
He said nobody would call it as huge as the crowd in the square they had once had.
By 1976 the logbook asked for nothing but something huge.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 huge 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1969 the fisherman wrote of a huge tree by the gate in the logbook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the hugest tree by the gate in the harbour, or so the logbook says.
My mother thought it too huge to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a huge crowd in the square, and nobody argued with him.
The boatman from the next harbour called the plan quite huge, and everybody laughed.
The huge ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
